questions.question: Pipes A and B together can fill a cistern in 10 hours. Pipes B and C together can fill the same cistern in 20 hours, and pipes C and A together can fill it in 12 hours. Find the time taken by pipe B alone to fill the cistern.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the total capacity of the **cistern** be the **LCM** of (10, 20, 12) = 60 units.

Combined **Efficiency**: (A+B) = 6, (B+C) = 3, (C+A) = 5.

Summing them: 2(A+B+C) = 6 + 3 + 5 = 14 ⇒ A+B+C = 7 units/hr.

Efficiency of **Pipe B** = (A+B+C) − (C+A) = 7 − 5 = 2 units/hr.

Time taken by B = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by (**Pipe A** + **Pipe B**) = 10 hr

Time taken by (**Pipe B** + **Pipe C**) = 20 hr

Time taken by (**Pipe C** + **Pipe A**) = 12 hr

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken

 
 

 **Pipes**
 **Time (hr)**
 **Total Work (LCM)**
 **Efficiency (units/hr)**
 
 

 A + B
 10
 60
 60 ÷ 10 = 6
 
 

 B + C
 20
 60 ÷ 20 = 3
 
 

 C + A
 12
 60 ÷ 12 = 5
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Adding efficiencies: (A + B) + (B + C) + (C + A) = 6 + 3 + 5

⇒ 2(A + B + C) = 14

⇒ A + B + C = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 units/hr

⇒ We know efficiency of (C + A) = 5 units/hr

⇒ Efficiency of B = (A + B + C) − (C + A) = 7 − 5 = 2 units/hr

⇒ Time taken by **Pipe B** alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of B

⇒ Time = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 hr

**∴ The correct answer is 30 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combined Efficiency Rule

When pipes work in pairs, the sum of their individual efficiencies is half the sum of their pairwise efficiencies: (A+B+C) = [(A+B) + (B+C) + (C+A)] ÷ 2.

Pipes and Cisterns Basics

Inlet pipes perform positive work (filling), while outlet pipes perform negative work (emptying). Total work is the volume of the tank/cistern.

Time and Work Relation

Time taken and efficiency are inversely proportional to each other. Time = 1 ÷ Efficiency (for constant work).

(A) Successive discounts of 21% and 8% on any number of toys bought.

(B) Successive discounts of 38%, 42% and 30% on any number of toys bought.

(C) 17% discount on the first 8 toys and 20% discount on each toy thereon.

(D) 7 toys free of cost on buying 10 toys.

A customer wants to buy 10 toys. Which of the above schemes is the least beneficial to her?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Approximate **Effective Discount** for each **Scheme**:

(A) 21 + 8 − (21 × 8 / 100) = 27.32%

(B) Successive 38%, 42%, 30% → clearly much higher than 50% (≈ 74.8%)

(C) Weighted Average = [(8 × 17) + (2 × 20)] ÷ 10 = 17.6%

(D) Buy 10 Get 7 Free = [7 ÷ (10 + 7)] × 100 ≈ 41.18%

Comparing the values, 17.6% is the lowest discount, making it the **least beneficial**.

**∴ The correct answer is C.**

questions.question: Simplify: (0.25 × 1.6) ÷ (0.04 × 0.5)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert decimals to fractions for faster calculation: 0.25 = 1/4 and 0.5 = 1/2.

Numerator: (1/4) × 1.6 = 0.4

Denominator: 0.04 × (1/2) = 0.02

Result = 0.4 ÷ 0.02 = 40 ÷ 2 = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (0.25 × 1.6) ÷ (0.04 × 0.5)

**Method Used:** Apply the **BODMAS** rule (perform operations inside **Brackets** first).

⇒ Step 1 (First bracket): 0.25 × 1.6 = 0.400 = 0.4

⇒ Step 2 (Second bracket): 0.04 × 0.5 = 0.020 = 0.02

⇒ Step 3 (Division): 0.4 ÷ 0.02

⇒ To remove the decimal from the divisor, multiply both numerator and denominator by 100.

⇒ (0.4 × 100) ÷ (0.02 × 100) = 40 ÷ 2

⇒ Result = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It stands for **Brackets**, **Of**, **Division**, **Multiplication**, **Addition**, and **Subtraction**. Operations must be performed in this specific order to get the correct result.

Multiplying Decimals

Multiply the numbers as if they were whole numbers, then place the **decimal point** in the product so that it has the same number of decimal places as the sum of the decimal places in the factors.

Dividing by Decimals

Move the **decimal point** in the divisor to the right until it is a whole number, and move the decimal point in the dividend the same number of places to the right before dividing.

questions.question: A delivery van covers the first 100 km at 50 km/h, the next 150 km at 60 km/h, and the last 50 km at 40 km/h. What is the average speed for the entire journey (correct to two places of decimal)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Average Speed** = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Total Distance = 100 + 150 + 50 = **300 km**

Total Time = (100/50) + (150/60) + (50/40) = 2 + 2.5 + 1.25 = **5.75 hours**

Average Speed = 300 ÷ 5.75 ≈ **52.17 km/h**

**∴ The correct answer is 52.17 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance₁ = **100 km**, Speed₁ = **50 km/h**

Distance₂ = **150 km**, Speed₂ = **60 km/h**

Distance₃ = **50 km**, Speed₃ = **40 km/h**

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Average Speed = (Total Distance) ÷ (Total Time)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/580f7114fc3d98426149780fdda51e074ed4ad5fca17a5cf8a20902eb8fa2037.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time for first part (t₁) = 100 ÷ 50 = **2 hours**

⇒ Time for second part (t₂) = 150 ÷ 60 = **2.5 hours**

⇒ Time for third part (t₃) = 50 ÷ 40 = 1.25 hours

⇒ Total Time (T) = 2 + 2.5 + 1.25 = **5.75 hours**

⇒ Average Speed = 300 ÷ 5.75

⇒ Average Speed = 30000 ÷ 575 = 1200 ÷ 23

⇒ Average Speed ≈ **52.1739... km/h**

**∴ The correct answer is 52.17 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Distances

When a journey is divided into two equal distances with speeds x and y, the Average Speed is the harmonic mean: (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Average Speed for Equal Time Intervals

If an object travels at speed x for time T and then at speed y for the same time T, the Average Speed is the arithmetic mean: (x + y) ÷ 2.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: Three numbers are in the ratio 3 : 7 : 2, and their LCM is 8820. Their HCF is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **HCF** of the three numbers be x.

The numbers are then 3x, 7x, and 2x.

**LCM** of (3x, 7x, 2x) = x × LCM(3, 7, 2) = x × 42.

Given, 42x = 8820.

x = 8820 ÷ 42 = 210.

**∴ The correct answer is 210.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Ratio** of three numbers = 3 : 7 : 2

**LCM** of the numbers = 8820

**Formula Used:**

If numbers are in the ratio a : b : c, then the numbers can be represented as ax, bx, and cx, where **x** is their **HCF**.

The **LCM** of these numbers = x × LCM(a, b, c).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d43a29f9718bde74149bb25db87b12bec41c42a4b9a404263fc0325c5224ffde.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the numbers be 3x, 7x, and 2x.

⇒ LCM(3, 7, 2) = 3 × 7 × 2 = 42 (as they are co-prime).

⇒ LCM of (3x, 7x, 2x) = 42x.

⇒ 42x = 8820.

⇒ x = 8820 ÷ 42.

⇒ x = 210.

**∴ The correct answer is 210.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF (Highest Common Factor)

The greatest number that divides two or more numbers without leaving a remainder.

LCM (Least Common Multiple)

The smallest non-zero number that is a multiple of two or more numbers.

Product Rule for Two Numbers

For any two numbers A and B: A × B = HCF(A, B) × LCM(A, B).

Co-prime Numbers

Two or more numbers are co-prime if their **HCF** is 1. Their **LCM** is simply the product of the numbers.

questions.question: If the interest on a sum of ₹y at 4% per annum compounded annually for 2 years is ₹765, then the total amount payable at the end of the two-year period will be _________.
questions.solution:

**Effective Interest Rate** for 2 years at 4% = 4 + 4 + (4 × 4)/100 = 8.16%.

Given that 8.16% of the **Principal** (y) = ₹765.

The **Total Amount** (A) percentage = 100% + 8.16% = 108.16%.

⇒ Amount = (765 ÷ 8.16) × 108.16

⇒ Amount = 93.75 × 108.16 = ₹10,140.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹10,140.**

questions.question: Sangeeta’s salary is revised twice in two consecutive years. In the first year, the salary is increased by 12%. In the second year, it is decreased by 10%. Despite this, her salary after the second revision is ₹1,584 more than the original salary. What is Sangeeta’s original monthly salary (in ₹)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net percentage change = a + b + (ab ÷ 100)

Here, a = +12% and b = −10%

Net change = 12 − 10 + (12 × (−10) ÷ 100) = 2 − 1.2 = 0.8%

Given, 0.8% increase = ₹1,584

Original Salary (100%) = (1,584 ÷ 0.8) × 100 = 1,980 × 100 = ₹1,98,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,98,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First year revision = **increased by 12%**

Second year revision = **decreased by 10%**

Increase in **original monthly salary** = **₹1,584**

**Formula Used:**

Final Value = Initial Value × (1 + r₁/100) × (1 + r₂/100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ec0cd04c3b047ef5f87c216a13789dbb6871647c5558eb55391f00fbb6b1c624.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let **Sangeeta's salary** be ₹x.

⇒ Salary after 1st year = x × (112 ÷ 100) = 1.12x

⇒ Salary after 2nd year = 1.12x × (90 ÷ 100) = 1.008x

⇒ Total increase in salary = 1.008x − x = 0.008x

⇒ 0.008x = 1,584

⇒ x = 1,584 ÷ 0.008

⇒ x = 1,584,000 ÷ 8

⇒ x = 1,98,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,98,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is changed by a% and then by b%, the net effective change is (a + b + ab/100)%.

Multiplying Factor Method

For an increase of r%, the factor is (1 + r/100). For a decrease, the factor is (1 − r/100). Final value = Initial value × Factor₁ × Factor₂.

Base Value Property

Percentage changes are always calculated on the preceding value in a series of successive changes, not on the original base value each time.

questions.question: In a college, the ratio of science to arts students is different for each of its three batches. In Batch A, the ratio is 5:8, in Batch B it is 7:11, and in Batch C it is 3:5. Which batch has the highest proportion of science students?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert **science-to-total** ratios into decimals to compare proportions:

**Batch A**: 5 ÷ (5 + 8) = 5/13 ≈ 0.3846

**Batch B**: 7 ÷ (7 + 11) = 7/18 ≈ 0.3888

**Batch C**: 3 ÷ (3 + 5) = 3/8 = 0.3750

Since 0.3888 > 0.3846 > 0.3750, **Batch B** has the highest proportion.

**∴ The correct answer is Batch B.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of **Science** to **Arts** students:

**Batch A** = 5 : 8 | **Batch B** = 7 : 11 | **Batch C** = 3 : 5

**Formula Used:**

**Proportion of Science students** = **Science** ÷ (**Science** + **Arts**)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3369ad8497fd77037e508911943f50e3376cf07bc4cd94560c1b133648c8cd88.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Batch A proportion** = 5 / (5 + 8) = 5/13

⇒ **Batch B proportion** = 7 / (7 + 11) = 7/18

⇒ **Batch C proportion** = 3 / (3 + 5) = 3/8

⇒ Comparing 5/13 and 7/18 by **cross-multiplication**: 5 × 18 = 90 and 7 × 13 = 91. Since 91 > 90, **Batch B** > **Batch A**.

⇒ Comparing 7/18 and 3/8 by **cross-multiplication**: 7 × 8 = 56 and 3 × 18 = 54. Since 56 > 54, **Batch B** > **Batch C**.

⇒ **Batch B** has the highest proportion of **science students**.

**∴ The correct answer is Batch B.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio to Proportion Conversion

If the ratio of two components is a:b, the proportion of the first component in the total is given by a/(a+b).

Comparing Fractions Shortcut

To compare a/b and c/d without division, compare the products (a × d) and (b × c). If ad > bc, then a c/d.

Percentage Share

The percentage share of a component is (Value / Total) × 100, which is useful for comparing proportions across different group sizes.

questions.question: If a man bought an article at 20% less than its marked price and sold it for ₹10 more than its marked price, his profit was 40%. What was the marked price (in ₹) of the article (correct to two decimal places)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **Marked Price (MP)** = 100 units.

**Cost Price (CP)** = 100 − 20% = 80 units.

**Selling Price (SP)** = 80 + 40% of 80 = 112 units.

Difference (SP − MP) = 112 − 100 = 12 units → ₹10.

**Marked Price** = (10 ÷ 12) × 100 = 1000 ÷ 12 = 83.33.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹83.33.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Discount on **Marked Price** = 20%

**Selling Price (SP)** = **Marked Price (MP)** + ₹10

**Profit Percentage** = 40%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/57f84556cc214964e6cce7522cb0aebdafa18b67ca512176ef9a26cbf290c194.png] 

⇒ Let the **Marked Price** be x.

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** = x − 20% of x = 0.8x.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = x + 10.

⇒ **Profit** = **SP** − **CP** = (x + 10) − 0.8x = 0.2x + 10.

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = (Profit ÷ **CP**) × 100

⇒ 40 = [(0.2x + 10) ÷ 0.8x] × 100

⇒ 0.40 = (0.2x + 10) ÷ 0.8x

⇒ 0.32x = 0.2x + 10

⇒ 0.12x = 10

⇒ x = 10 ÷ 0.12 = 83.333...

**∴ The correct answer is ₹83.33.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship between CP and MP

The direct ratio between **Cost Price** and **Marked Price** is given by: CP/MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%).

Successive Discounts

Two successive discounts of a% and b% are equivalent to a single discount of [a + b − (a × b)/100]%.

Mark-up Percentage

Mark-up % = [(MP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100. It represents how much more the **Marked Price** is compared to the **Cost Price**.

questions.question: The amount under simple interest on a sum of ₹8,000 for 3 years at an interest rate of 7.5% per annum is
questions.solution:

Amount = 122.5% of **₹8,000**

Amount = 1.225 × 8000 = **₹9,800**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI)

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = (8000 × 7.5 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 80 × 22.5

⇒ SI = **₹1,800**

Simple Interest Concept

Simple Interest is calculated only on the initial principal amount throughout the entire period. SI = P × R × T / 100.

Amount in SI

The total value after adding interest to the principal is called the Amount. A = P(1 + RT/100).

SI vs CI Difference

For the first year, SI and Compound Interest (CI) are equal if interest is compounded annually. From the second year, CI > SI because interest is earned on interest.

questions.question: Which of the following ratios is equal to 3:2?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert the given target ratio 3:2 into decimal form: 3 ÷ 2 = **1.5**.

Check the decimal values of the options:

60/45 ≈ 1.33 | 45/20 = 2.25 | 35/25 = 1.4 | 120/80 = **1.5**.

Since 120/80 matches the decimal value 1.5, it is equivalent to 3:2.

**∴ The correct answer is 120:80.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Target Ratio = 3 : 2

**Formula Used:** Simplest form of a ratio is obtained by dividing both terms by their **Highest Common Factor (HCF)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/78233d0b10acc86988b3a6be5947a346d4bf7d83c31a9a43c518040c4ce1e8f1.png] 

⇒ Option 1: 60 : 45 (HCF = 15) ⇒ (60 ÷ 15) : (45 ÷ 15) = 4 : 3

⇒ Option 2: 45 : 20 (HCF = 5) ⇒ (45 ÷ 5) : (20 ÷ 5) = 9 : 4

⇒ Option 3: 35 : 25 (HCF = 5) ⇒ (35 ÷ 5) : (25 ÷ 5) = 7 : 5

⇒ Option 4: 120 : 80 (HCF = 40) ⇒ (120 ÷ 40) : (80 ÷ 40) = 3 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 120:80.**

Simplest Form of Ratio

A ratio a:b is in its **simplest form** if the HCF of a and b is 1. To simplify, divide both terms by their common factors.

Equivalent Ratios

Ratios that represent the same relationship between numbers are called **equivalent ratios**. They can be found by multiplying or dividing both terms by the same non-zero number.

Proportion

When two ratios are equal, they are said to be in **proportion**. For a:b = c:d, the product of extremes (a×d) equals the product of means (b×c).

questions.question: A ladder leans against a wall, making an angle of 60° with the ground. If the foot of the ladder is 15 metres from the wall, what is the length of the ladder?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **30°−60°−90°** right-angled triangle, the sides are in the ratio **1 : √3 : 2**.

The base (adjacent to 60°) corresponds to **1 unit**.

Given, 1 unit = **15 m**.

The ladder (hypotenuse) corresponds to **2 units**.

Length of ladder = 2 × 15 = **30 m**.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Angle of elevation of the **ladder** with the ground (θ) = 60°

Distance of the foot of the ladder from the **wall** (Base) = 15 m

**Formula Used:**

In a right-angled triangle, cos θ = Base / Hypotenuse

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/937ffc1bf0b80f770fc8c14c96721593051ef2397d4bf0c4d2cdebe86e04c505.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the length of the ladder be **L**.

⇒ cos 60° = 15 / L

⇒ 1 / 2 = 15 / L

⇒ L = 15 × 2

⇒ L = 30 m

**∴ The correct answer is 30 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

Fundamental ratios in a right triangle: **sin θ** = P/H, **cos θ** = B/H, and **tan θ** = P/B (where P = Perpendicular, B = Base, H = Hypotenuse).

Standard Values of Cosine

Common values include cos 0° = 1, cos 30° = √3/2, cos 45° = 1/√2, **cos 60° = 1/2**, and cos 90° = 0.

Pythagoras Theorem

In any right-angled triangle, the relationship between the sides is given by **H² = P² + B²**.

30-60-90 Triangle Rule

For a triangle with angles 30°, 60°, and 90°, the side lengths are always in the ratio **x : x√3 : 2x**.

questions.question: A train covers a distance of 300 kilometers in 5 hours. If the same train takes 6 hours to cover the same distance, what is the change in its speed?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When **Distance** is constant, **Speed** is inversely proportional to **Time**.

Ratio of **Time** = 5 : 6 → Ratio of **Speed** = 6 : 5.

Original **Speed** = 300 ÷ 5 = 60 km/h.

Here, 6 units = 60 km/h ⇒ 1 unit (change) = 10 km/h.

Since the ratio decreases from 6 to 5, the speed decreases.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 km/h decrease.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Distance** (D) = 300 km

**Initial Time** (T₁) = 5 hr

**New Time** (T₂) = 6 hr

**Formula Used:**

**Speed** (S) = **Distance** (D) ÷ **Time** (T)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8cb93995fc424390cfa7ff88c7db3dfd49205e9ca031c7593a25f99d1ec9cc93.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Initial Speed** (S₁) = 300 ÷ 5 = 60 km/h

⇒ **New Speed** (S₂) = 300 ÷ 6 = 50 km/h

⇒ Change in **Speed** = **Initial Speed** − **New Speed**

⇒ Change = 60 − 50 = 10 km/h

⇒ Since the new speed is lower, there is a **decrease** of 10 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 km/h decrease.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed-Time Relation

For a fixed distance, Speed and Time are inversely proportional. If time increases by a certain factor, speed must decrease by the same factor to cover the same distance.

Average Speed

**Average Speed** is calculated as the **Total Distance** divided by the **Total Time** taken for the entire journey. Formula: Average Speed = (Total Distance) ÷ (Total Time).

Unit Conversion

To convert **Speed** from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/h, multiply the value by 18/5.

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 11?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A number is **divisible by 11** if the difference between the **sum of digits at odd places** and the **sum of digits at even places** is 0 or a multiple of 11.

Check 3,762: (2 + 7) − (6 + 3) = 9 − 9 = 0.

Since the result is 0, the number **3,762** is divisible by 11.

**∴ The correct answer is 3,762.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers are 3,762, 7,393, 4,915, and 6,184.

**Divisibility Rule of 11:** Let the digits of a number be checked from right to left. The difference (Sum of digits at positions 1, 3, 5...) − (Sum of digits at positions 2, 4, 6...) must be 0, 11, 22, etc.

⇒ For **3,762**: (2 + 7) − (6 + 3) = 9 − 9 = 0 (Divisible)

⇒ For **7,393**: (3 + 3) − (9 + 7) = 6 − 16 = −10 (Not divisible)

⇒ For **4,915**: (5 + 9) − (1 + 4) = 14 − 5 = 9 (Not divisible)

⇒ For **6,184**: (4 + 1) − (8 + 6) = 5 − 14 = −9 (Not divisible)

**∴ The correct answer is 3,762.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 3 and 9

A number is divisible by **3** or **9** if the **sum of its digits** is divisible by 3 or 9, respectively.

Divisibility by 4

A number is divisible by **4** if the **last two digits** of the number are divisible by 4.

Divisibility by 8

A number is divisible by **8** if the **last three digits** of the number are divisible by 8.

questions.question: Evaluate 23³ + (-14)³ + (-9)³
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check if the **sum of terms** is zero: 23 + (−14) + (−9) = 23 − 23 = 0.

Apply the **Algebraic Identity**: If a + b + c = 0, then a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc.

Calculation: 3 × 23 × (−14) × (−9) = 3 × 23 × 126.

Result: 69 × 126 = 8694.

**∴ The correct answer is 8694.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

a = 23

b = −14

c = −9

**Formula Used:**

a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, evaluate the sum **(a + b + c)**:

⇒ 23 + (−14) + (−9) = 23 − 14 − 9 = 0

⇒ Since the sum is **zero**, the right side of the identity becomes zero.

⇒ a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = 0 × (a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca) = 0

⇒ a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc

⇒ Substitute the values: 3 × 23 × (−14) × (−9)

⇒ 3 × 23 × 126

⇒ 69 × 126 = 8694

**∴ The correct answer is 8694.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Conditional Algebraic Identity

The identity a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc holds true if and only if **a + b + c = 0** or **a = b = c**.

General Expansion

The expression a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca can be rewritten as 1/2[(a−b)² + (b−c)² + (c−a)²], which is always non-negative for real numbers.

Trinomial Square

Another useful identity is (a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca).

questions.question: The population of a town increases by 10% in the year 2015 and decreases by 15% in the year 2016. If the population of the town at the end of the year 2016 is 1,87,000, find the population of the town in the beginning of the year 2015.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Ratio Method** for successive changes:

Year 2015 (10% increase): 10 → 11

Year 2016 (15% decrease): 20 → 17 (since 15% = 3/20)

Overall Ratio: (10 × 20) : (11 × 17) = 200 : 187

Given final value: 187 units = 1,87,000 ⇒ 1 unit = 1,000

Initial Population = 200 × 1,000 = 2,00,000

**∴ The correct answer is 2,00,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9233f1b153b216173dcbb678069f1107e7b791b362bfe9c0b46700689aaf598f.png] 

Let the **Initial Population** in the beginning of 2015 be **P**.

⇒ Population after 10% increase in 2015 = P × (1 + 10/100) = 1.1P

⇒ Population after 15% decrease in 2016 = 1.1P × (1 − 15/100)

⇒ Population at the end of 2016 = 1.1P × 0.85 = 0.935P

⇒ According to the question: 0.935P = 1,87,000

⇒ P = 1,87,000 ÷ 0.935

⇒ P = (1,87,000 × 1,000) ÷ 935

⇒ P = 200 × 1,000 = 2,00,000

**∴ The correct answer is 2,00,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change Formula

For two successive changes of a% and b%, the effective net change is [a + b + (a × b)/100]%. Use positive for increase and negative for decrease.

Multiplier Method

Final Value = Initial Value × (1 ± r₁/100) × (1 ± r₂/100). This is widely used in population growth and depreciation problems.

Population Growth

If the population increases at a constant rate r% per annum, the population after n years is P(1 + r/100)ⁿ.

questions.question: A pair of shoes is marked at ₹2800 and is subject to a trade discount of 18%. Under a special offer, a customer buys 5 pairs at the discounted price and gets an additional 2 pairs at 50% off the discounted price. Find the total cost to the customer for 7 pairs of shoes.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Marked Price** per pair = ₹2800.

Discounted Price (DP) per pair = 82% of 2800 = ₹2296.

Special offer allows 5 pairs at full DP and 2 pairs at 50% DP (which is 1 pair at full DP).

Total effective cost for 7 pairs = (5 + 1) × 2296 = 6 × 2296.

Total Cost = ₹13,776.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹13,776.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Marked Price (MP)** of a pair of shoes = ₹2800

**Trade Discount** = 18%

Quantity 1 = 5 pairs at discounted price

Quantity 2 = 2 pairs at 50% of discounted price

**Formula Used:**

Discounted Price = MP × (100 − Discount%) / 100

Total Cost = (Quantity₁ × Price₁) + (Quantity₂ × Price₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ed2016944b14114cb8c745209140d573745b3d23d99c99055b1f78866acc9a8c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Trade Discount** amount = 18% of 2800 = 0.18 × 2800 = ₹504

⇒ **Discounted Price (DP)** per pair = 2800 − 504 = ₹2296

⇒ Cost of first 5 pairs = 5 × 2296 = ₹11,480

⇒ Cost of next 2 pairs = 2 × (50% of 2296) = 2 × 1148 = ₹2,296

⇒ **Total Cost** for 7 pairs = 11480 + 2296 = ₹13,776

**∴ The correct answer is ₹13,776.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Selling Price

Successive Discounts

Trade Discount vs Cash Discount

Trade discount is given on the list price at the time of sale, while cash discount is offered for immediate or early payment.

questions.question: The average monthly income of six employees in an office is ₹24,000. When a new employee joins the office, the average income of all seven employees becomes ₹25,500. What is the monthly income of the new employee?

Income = 25,500 + (6 × 1,500) = 25,500 + 9,000 = ₹34,500.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹34,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Initial number of employees = 6 | Initial **average income** = ₹24,000

Final number of employees = 7 | Final **average income** = ₹25,500

Total Income = **Average Income** × **Number of Employees**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8ef2831966339583ca54b507721b426f3fe26cdce81c153d11ce58213546ba59.png]

⇒ Total monthly income of 6 employees = 6 × 24,000 = ₹1,44,000

⇒ Monthly income of the **new employee** = Total (7 employees) − Total (6 employees)

⇒ Monthly income = 1,78,500 − 1,44,000 = ₹34,500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹34,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

The sum of deviations of all observations from their **arithmetic mean** is always zero.

Weighted Average

When two groups are combined, the **combined average** is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Inclusion and Exclusion

If adding a new member **increases** the average, the new member's value is **higher** than the original average.

questions.question: In a division sum, the divisor is 14 times the quotient and 5 times the remainder. If the remainder is 56, what is the dividend?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Divisor** = 5 × **Remainder** = 5 × 56 = 280

**Quotient** = **Divisor** ÷ 14 = 280 ÷ 14 = 20

**Dividend** = (**Divisor** × **Quotient**) + **Remainder**

**Dividend** = (280 × 20) + 56 = 5600 + 56 = 5656

**∴ The correct answer is 5656.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Remainder** (r) = 56

**Divisor** (d) = 5 × **Remainder**

**Divisor** (d) = 14 × **Quotient** (q)

**Formula Used:**

**Dividend** = (**Divisor** × **Quotient**) + **Remainder**

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Divisor** = 5 × 56 = 280

⇒ 14 × **Quotient** = 280

⇒ **Quotient** = 280 ÷ 14 = 20

⇒ **Dividend** = (280 × 20) + 56

⇒ **Dividend** = 5600 + 56

⇒ **Dividend** = 5656

**∴ The correct answer is 5656.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Division Algorithm

For any two whole numbers, the **dividend** is always equal to the product of the **divisor** and **quotient** plus the **remainder**.

Remainder Property

The **remainder** must always be greater than or equal to 0 and strictly less than the **divisor** (0 ≤ r < d).

Euclid's Division Lemma

It states that for any two positive integers a and b, there exist unique integers q and r such that a = bq + r.

questions.question: Sphere A has a radius of 6 cm and Sphere B has a radius of 3 cm. What is the ratio of the surface area of A to that of B?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **ratio of surface areas** of two spheres is equal to the **square of the ratio** of their radii.

Radius of Sphere A : Radius of Sphere B = 6 : 3 = 2 : 1

Surface Area Ratio = (2)² : (1)² = 4 : 1

**∴ The correct answer is 4:1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of **Sphere A** (r₁) = 6 cm

Radius of **Sphere B** (r₂) = 3 cm

**Formula Used:**

Surface Area (S) of a sphere = 4πr²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9a376e70bc17bc435035b6c1300b8f4bf6c9c41b4778056796d32d23ca880d98.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Surface Area of Sphere A (S₁) = 4 × π × (6)²

⇒ S₁ = 4 × π × 36 = 144π cm²

⇒ Surface Area of Sphere B (S₂) = 4 × π × (3)²

⇒ S₂ = 4 × π × 9 = 36π cm²

⇒ Ratio = S₁ : S₂ = 144π : 36π

⇒ Ratio = 144 / 36 = 4 / 1

**∴ The correct answer is 4:1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Sphere

The volume (V) of a sphere is given by the formula V = (4/3)πr³.

Ratio of Volumes

The ratio of the **volumes** of two spheres is equal to the **cube of the ratio** of their radii: V₁/V₂ = (r₁/r₂)³.

Hemisphere Properties

For a hemisphere, the Curved Surface Area = 2πr² and the Total Surface Area = 3πr².

questions.question: Eight mangoes and five oranges cost ₹164, while five mangoes and eight oranges cost ₹148. Determine the cost of three mangoes and three oranges.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Summing both conditions: (8 + 5) **Mangoes** + (5 + 8) **Oranges** = 164 + 148

⇒ 13 (Mangoes + Oranges) = ₹312

⇒ 1 (Mango + Orange) = 312 ÷ 13 = ₹24

⇒ 3 (Mangoes + Oranges) = 3 × 24 = ₹72

**∴ The correct answer is ₹72.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost of **8 mangoes** and **5 oranges** = ₹164

Cost of **5 mangoes** and **8 oranges** = ₹148

**Formula Used:**

**Symmetrical Linear Equations**: Add equations when coefficients are interchanged.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8839673c9ed4ad9c50401a6c8ac0d179995bbc122ebdde897cde0bfa5b1b2a30.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let cost of 1 mango be **M** and 1 orange be **O**.

⇒ 8M + 5O = 164 --- (Equation 1)

⇒ 5M + 8O = 148 --- (Equation 2)

⇒ Adding Eq(1) and Eq(2): (8M + 5M) + (5O + 8O) = 164 + 148

⇒ 13M + 13O = 312

⇒ 13(M + O) = 312

⇒ M + O = 312 ÷ 13 = 24

⇒ Cost of 3 mangoes and 3 oranges = 3 × (M + O)

⇒ 3 × 24 = 72

**∴ The correct answer is ₹72.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Equations in Two Variables

Symmetrical Coefficients Property

When coefficients are interchanged (ax + by = m and bx + ay = n), adding them directly gives a simplified value for (x + y).

Unitary Method

A problem-solving technique where you first find the value of a single unit and then multiply it by the required quantity.

questions.question:
The mean of the following data is 12.5. Find the missing frequency p.

Data Values (x): 10, 15

Frequency (f): 5, p
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a distribution with two values, the **mean** acts as the **balance point**.

Difference between first value (10) and mean (12.5) = 12.5 − 10 = 2.5

Difference between second value (15) and mean (12.5) = 15 − 12.5 = 2.5

Since the **deviations** are equal in magnitude (2.5), the **frequencies** must also be **equal**.

Given first frequency = 5, therefore **p = 5**.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Mean (χ) = 12.5

Values (xᵢ): 10, 15

Frequencies (fᵢ): 5, p

**Formula Used:**

Arithmetic Mean (χ) = ∑fᵢxᵢ ÷ ∑fᵢ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/02486fc1000efeedc9dfdc0577de97cc6304cb94287f190d384c578840b76f57.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 12.5 = (10 × 5 + 15 × p) ÷ (5 + p)

⇒ 12.5 × (5 + p) = 50 + 15p

⇒ 62.5 + 12.5p = 50 + 15p

⇒ 62.5 − 50 = 15p − 12.5p

⇒ 12.5 = 2.5p

⇒ p = 12.5 ÷ 2.5

⇒ p = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Arithmetic Mean

The algebraic sum of **deviations** of a set of observations from their **arithmetic mean** is always **zero**. ∑fᵢ(xᵢ − χ) = 0.

Weighted Average Formula

When different values have different importance or frequency, the **weighted mean** is calculated as χw = (w₁x₁ + w₂x₂ + ... + wₙxₙ) ÷ (w₁ + w₂ + ... + wₙ).

Change of Origin and Scale

If every observation is increased by 'a', the **mean** increases by 'a'. If every observation is multiplied by 'k', the **mean** is multiplied by 'k'.

questions.question: If the third proportional to 4 and 20 is m and the third proportional to m and 50 is n, what is the value of n?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Third Proportional** of **a** and **b** is calculated as **b² ÷ a**.

First, find **m**: **m** = (20 × 20) ÷ 4 = 100.

Then, find **n**: **n** = (50 × 50) ÷ 100 = 25.

**∴ The correct answer is 25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First pair: **4**, **20** and **m** are in continuous proportion.

Second pair: **m**, **50** and **n** are in continuous proportion.

**Formula Used:**

If **a**, **b**, **c** are in continuous proportion, then **a : b = b : c** ⇒ **c = b² ÷ a**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/abaa1205711701ca48686190c7dbd88e0b6f57d80571c92a87b2f69adf4ef064.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ For the first set: 4 : 20 = 20 : **m**

⇒ **m** = (20 × 20) ÷ 4

⇒ **m** = 400 ÷ 4 = **100**

⇒ For the second set: 100 : 50 = 50 : **n**

⇒ **n** = (50 × 50) ÷ 100

⇒ **n** = 2500 ÷ 100 = **25**

**∴ The correct answer is 25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers **a** and **b** is calculated as **√(a × b)**.

Fourth Proportional

If four numbers **a**, **b**, **c**, and **d** are in proportion (**a : b :: c : d**), then the fourth proportional **d** = **(b × c) ÷ a**.

Continued Proportion

Three numbers are in **continued proportion** if the ratio of the first to the second is equal to the ratio of the second to the third (**a/b = b/c**).

questions.question: In which state of India are the three crops of rice — called ‘aus,’ ‘aman,’ and ‘boro’ — grown?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**West Bengal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In India, particularly in states like **West Bengal**, **Assam**, and **Odisha**, the prevailing climatic conditions allow for the cultivation of three distinct crops of rice within a single agricultural year.
 
• The three varieties are identified based on their seasonal cycles and are locally named **Aus**, **Aman**, and **Boro**.
 
• **Aman** is the primary **winter rice** crop. It is typically sown during the onset of the **Southwest Monsoon** in June and July and harvested between November and December. It occupies the largest portion of the total rice area in the state.
 
• **Aus** is referred to as **autumn rice**. It is sown during the pre-monsoon period in May and June and harvested in the autumn months of September and October.
 
• **Boro** is known as **summer rice**. This variety is sown in the winter (November to January) and harvested in the summer (April to May). Its cultivation is heavily reliant on **assured irrigation** facilities during the dry season.
 
• The **fertile alluvial soil** and the hot, humid climate of the **lower Gangetic plains** in **West Bengal** provide the ideal environment for this intensive cropping pattern.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rice (Oryza sativa)**:

 
 
• It is the **staple food crop** for a significant majority of India’s population and is primarily a **Kharif crop**.
 
• Growth requires high temperatures (above **25°C**), high humidity, and annual rainfall exceeding **100 cm**.
 
• **West Bengal** is consistently among the top producers of rice in India, contributing significantly to the national **food security**.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Context of Other Options**:
 
 
• In **Manipur** and **Nagaland**, rice is often grown using **Jhum (shifting) cultivation** or **terrace farming** in hilly terrains, where a single crop is more common due to topographical constraints.
 
• While **Bihar** is a major rice producer, the specific nomenclature and systematic triple-cropping of **Aus, Aman, and Boro** are most traditionally associated with the **Bengal delta** region.

questions.question: Which national statistical organization is being changed by the Indian government's September 2025 draft bill ahead of its centenary?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Statistical Institute (ISI)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)** has introduced a draft bill to amend the **Indian Statistical Institute Act, 1959**, aiming to modernize the governance and administrative framework of the **Indian Statistical Institute (ISI)**.
 
• The **Indian Statistical Institute** was established by the legendary statistician **Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis** on **December 17, 1931**, and was later declared an **Institution of National Importance** by an Act of Parliament in **1959**.
 
• As the institute approaches its **centenary** year in **2031**, the government seeks to restructure its organizational hierarchy to enhance efficiency and accountability in its academic and research pursuits.
 
• A significant proposal in the draft bill includes the redesignation of the head of the institute from **Director** to **Director General**, bringing it in line with the leadership structure of other elite scientific and research organizations in **India**.
 
• The proposed legislation also focuses on reforming the **ISI Council**, which is the apex governing body, to improve the decision-making process and integrate modern management practices within the premier statistical body.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)** and **Central Statistics Office (CSO)**:

 
 
• The **NSSO** was previously responsible for conducting large-scale nationwide sample surveys on various socio-economic aspects.
 
• The **CSO** was the nodal agency for coordinating statistical activities and preparing **National Accounts**, including **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** estimates.
 
• In **May 2019**, the **Government of India** merged the **NSSO** and the **CSO** to form a unified **National Statistical Office (NSO)** under the **MoSPI**.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**:
 
 
• This ministry consists of two wings: the **Statistics Wing** (NSO) and the **Programme Implementation Wing**.
 
• It is responsible for the release of key economic indicators such as the **Index of Industrial Production (IIP)** and the **Consumer Price Index (CPI)**.
 
• The ministry also monitors the progress of **Central Sector Projects** costing 150 crore rupees and above.

• The **Government of Union Territories Act, 1963** was enacted by the Parliament to provide for **Legislative Assemblies** and **Councils of Ministers** for certain Union Territories (UTs).
 
• This Act was a direct consequence of the **14th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1962**, which introduced **Article 239A** to the Indian Constitution, allowing Parliament to create a local legislature for UTs.
 
• **Puducherry** (then Pondicherry) was officially granted its own legislature through this Act in **1963**, shortly after its **de jure** transfer from **French** administration to India.

__
 
• **Hampi**, situated on the southern bank of the **Tungabhadra River** in the state of **Karnataka**, served as the magnificent capital of the **Vijayanagara Empire** from **1336 to 1565 AD**.
 
• The empire was founded by two brothers, **Harihara I** and **Bukka Raya I**, belonging to the **Sangama Dynasty**, who established a stronghold against the expansion of the northern Sultanates.
 
• The city reached its cultural and territorial peak during the reign of **Krishnadevaraya** (1509–1529 AD), who is considered the most powerful ruler of the **Tuluva Dynasty**.
 
• **Hampi** was renowned globally for its architectural brilliance, featuring massive fortifications, complex **Dravidian-style** temples, and innovative urban planning including aqueducts and markets.
 
• The prosperity of the city came to a violent end in **1565** following the **Battle of Talikota**, where a coalition of **Deccan Sultanates** (Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmednagar, and Bidar) defeated and subsequently plundered the capital.
 
• In recognition of its historical and architectural significance, **UNESCO** designated the group of monuments at **Hampi** as a **World Heritage Site** in **1986**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• Often referred to as the **Golden Age of India** (4th to 6th century CE), its primary capital was located at **Pataliputra** (modern-day Patna).
 
• Known for advancements in **Sanskrit literature**, **astronomy**, and the **decimal system**.
 
 
 
• **Mughal Empire**:
 
 
• An empire of Central Asian origin established by **Babur** in **1526**.
 
• The empire’s prominent capitals included **Agra**, **Fatehpur Sikri**, and **Shahjahanabad** (Old Delhi).
 
 
 
• **Maurya Empire**:
 
 
• Founded by **Chandragupta Maurya** in **322 BCE**, it was the first pan-Indian empire.
 
• Its administrative center and capital was **Pataliputra**, and it is most famous for the reign of **Ashoka the Great**.
 
 
 
• **Virupaksha Temple**:
 
 
• One of the oldest structures in **Hampi**, dedicated to **Lord Shiva**, which remained an active place of worship even after the city was abandoned.

The correct answer is __**Railways**__.

• **Railways** serve as the principal mode of transportation for freight in India, particularly for **heavy and bulky goods** over long distances, due to their immense load-bearing capacity and cost-efficiency.
 
• The **Indian Railways** network is one of the largest in the world, spanning over **68,000 kilometers**, which allows for the seamless movement of materials between mineral-rich zones and industrial hubs.
 
• Bulk commodities like **coal**, **iron ore**, **cement**, **food grains**, and **fertilizers** constitute the majority of the freight traffic, as rail transport can carry massive volumes in a single trip compared to other modes.

• **Hathigumpha Inscription**: King **Kharavela** of the **Chedi Dynasty** (Mahameghavahana) of **Kalinga** inscribed his achievements in the **Hathigumpha Inscription** at **Udayagiri**, Odisha. This 17-line record is written in **Prakrit** using the **Brahmi script**.

• **Administrative Use**: During the **3rd and 2nd centuries BCE**, **Prakrit** served as the primary language for royal proclamations and administrative records, preceding the dominance of **Classical Sanskrit** in later centuries.

questions.question: What does PCB stand for in a Computer System?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Printed Circuit Board**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Printed Circuit Board (PCB)** is a rigid structure that physically supports and electrically connects **electronic components** using conductive pathways, tracks, or signal traces etched from **copper** sheets.
 
• In the context of a **Computer System**, the most significant PCB is the **Motherboard** (also known as the mainboard or system board), which serves as the backbone for connecting the **Central Processing Unit (CPU)**, **Random Access Memory (RAM)**, and all other internal hardware.
 
• PCBs are typically manufactured using a **non-conductive substrate** material, most frequently **FR-4**, which is a flame-retardant fiberglass-reinforced epoxy laminate.
 
• The primary function of a PCB is to ensure a stable **electrical connection** between components like **transistors**, **capacitors**, and **microprocessors**, while providing a compact and reliable layout for complex circuitry.
 
• The production of PCBs involves a process called **photolithography** or **chemical etching** to remove unwanted copper, leaving only the required circuit traces that define the **electronic architecture** of the device.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Structural Layers of a PCB**:

• **Silkscreen**: A layer of **ink traces** used to print labels, component identifiers (reference designators), and logos for easier maintenance and repair.
 
 
 
• **Process Control Block**:
 
 
• In the domain of **Operating Systems** (software), the acronym **PCB** can also refer to a **Process Control Block**, which is a data structure used by the **Kernel** to store information about a specific **active process**.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of Circuitry**:
 
 
• Before PCBs, circuits were built using **point-to-point wiring**, which was highly susceptible to **short circuits** and mechanical failure as complexity increased. The transition to PCBs allowed for the **miniaturization** of modern laptops, smartphones, and high-performance servers.

questions.question: Select the correct formula of Aluminium Sulphate.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Al₂(SO₄)₃**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The chemical formula of **Aluminium Sulphate** is determined using the **valency** or **oxidation state** of the constituent ions to ensure the resulting compound is **electrically neutral**.
 
• **Aluminium (Al)** is a group 13 element and typically forms a cation with a charge of **+3** (**Al³⁺**), meaning it loses three electrons to achieve a stable octet.
 
• The **Sulphate ion (SO₄)** is a polyatomic anion consisting of one sulphur atom and four oxygen atoms, carrying a collective charge of **-2** (**SO₄²−**).
 
• Applying the **criss-cross method**, the numerical value of the charge of the **Aluminium ion** (3) becomes the **subscript** for the **Sulphate ion**, and the numerical value of the charge of the **Sulphate ion** (2) becomes the **subscript** for the **Aluminium ion**.
 
• To balance the total charge: **2 × (+3) + 3 × (−2) = 0**. Therefore, two aluminium atoms combine with three sulphate groups to form **Al₂(SO₄)₃**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Properties and Characteristics**:

 
 
• **Molar Mass**: The anhydrous form of **Aluminium Sulphate** has a molar mass of approximately **342.15 g/mol**.
 
• **Physical Appearance**: It usually appears as a **white crystalline solid** or powder and is highly **hygroscopic**, meaning it readily absorbs moisture from the air.
 
• **Solubility**: It is **highly soluble in water** but virtually insoluble in **ethanol**. When dissolved in water, it undergoes hydrolysis to form an **acidic solution**.
 
• **Industrial Uses**:
 
 
• **Water Purification**: It acts as a **coagulant**, causing impurities to clump together (flocculation) so they can be easily filtered out.
 
• **Paper Industry**: Used as a **sizing agent** to adjust the paper's absorbency and improve its printability.
 
• **Textile Dyeing**: Functions as a **mordant**, helping dyes adhere to fabric fibers like cotton.

questions.question: Which Indian Constitutional Amendment Act has inserted the word ‘socialist’ into the Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**42nd Constitutional Amendment Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act**, enacted in **1976** during the **Internal Emergency** under the **Indira Gandhi** administration, is the most extensive amendment in the history of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• This amendment is famously known as the **Mini-Constitution** because it introduced massive changes to the **constitutional structure**, including the **Preamble**, **Fundamental Rights**, and **Directive Principles**.
 
• For the first and only time since the adoption of the Constitution, the **Preamble** was amended to include three new terms: **Socialist**, **Secular**, and **Integrity**.
 
• The insertion of the word **Socialist** was intended to emphasize the **egalitarian** goals of the Indian state, specifically **Democratic Socialism**, which aims to end poverty, ignorance, disease, and inequality of opportunity.
 
• The addition of **Socialist** formally aligned the **Preamble** with the **Directive Principles of State Policy**, particularly **Article 39**, which seeks the equitable distribution of material resources.
 
• Unlike the **communistic socialism** of the Soviet model, **Indian Socialism** is a **Gandhian-Marxist** blend that favors a **mixed economy** where the private and public sectors co-exist.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **38th Constitutional Amendment Act (1975)**:

 
 
• Empowered the **President** to declare a state of **Emergency** that would be non-justiciable in a court of law.
 
• Ensured that **Ordinances** promulgated by the President or Governors could not be challenged in court.
 
 
 
• **44th Constitutional Amendment Act (1978)**:
 
 
• Enacted by the **Janata Government** to undo several controversial changes brought by the **42nd Amendment**.
 
• It removed the **Right to Property** from the list of **Fundamental Rights** and made it a **Legal Right** under **Article 300A**.
 
 
 
• **86th Constitutional Amendment Act (2002)**:
 
 
• Inserted **Article 21A**, making **Free and Compulsory Education** a Fundamental Right for children aged **6 to 14 years**.
 
• Added a new **Fundamental Duty** under **Article 51A(k)** for parents and guardians.

questions.question: Which of the following is a correct match of a climate type with its vegetation or features as per Koeppen's scheme of classification of climate?

options.text: Aw – Deciduous forests and tree-shredded grasslands

__
 
• **BWh** represents the **Subtropical Hot Desert climate**. The letter **B** stands for arid climates, **W** for desert (Wüste), and **h** for hot. This climate is characterized by high temperatures and extremely low precipitation, supporting **xerophytic vegetation** like cacti and thorny bushes rather than a **dense evergreen canopy**. Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.
 
• **ET** stands for the **Tundra climate** within the **Polar (E)** group. In this climate, the average temperature of the warmest month is between **0°C** and **10°C**. The vegetation consists of **mosses, lichens, and stunted shrubs**, while **tropical rainforests** are associated with the **Af** climate. Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.
 
• **Aw** denotes the **Tropical Savanna climate**. It is defined by a distinct **dry season** (usually in winter) and a wet season. The vegetation comprises **deciduous forests** that shed leaves during the dry period and **grasslands** interspersed with trees (often referred to as **savanna**). Hence, statement 3 is correct.
 
• **Cfa** refers to the **Humid Subtropical climate**, characterized by hot, humid summers and mild winters with rainfall occurring throughout the year. **Cold deserts (BWk)** and **permafrost (EF/ET)** are found in much colder or more arid latitudinal zones. Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Koeppen Climate Classification System**: Developed by **Wladimir Koeppen** in 1884, it categorizes climates based on monthly and annual averages of **temperature** and **precipitation**.

 
 
• **Group A (Tropical Humid)**: Tropical climates where the average temperature of every month is **18°C** or higher.

 
 
• **Af**: Tropical Wet (Rainforest).
 
• **Am**: Tropical Monsoon.
 
• **Aw**: Tropical Wet and Dry (Savanna).
 
 
 
• **Group B (Dry Climates)**: Regions where potential **evapotranspiration** exceeds precipitation.
 
 
• **BSh**: Semi-arid Steppe.
 
• **BWk**: Mid-latitude Cold Desert.
 
 
 
• **Group C (Warm Temperate)**: Mid-latitude climates with mild winters; the coldest month average is between **−3°C** and **18°C**.

questions.question: The stomach secretes the enzyme pepsin to aid digestion. Pepsin mainly acts on which nutrient?

• **Pepsin** is a powerful enzyme found in **Gastric Juice** that initiates the digestion of proteins by breaking them down into smaller units called **Peptones** and **Proteoses**.
 
• It is secreted by the **Chief Cells** (peptic cells) of the stomach lining in an inactive proenzyme form known as **Pepsinogen**.
 
• The activation of **Pepsinogen** into **Pepsin** requires an acidic medium, which is provided by **Hydrochloric Acid (HCl)** secreted by the **Oxyntic Cells** (parietal cells).
 
• The stomach maintains a highly acidic **pH** level (approximately 1.8), which is the optimum environment for **Pepsin** to function efficiently as an **Endopeptidase**.

• Requires **Emulsification** by **Bile Salts** produced in the **Liver** and stored in the **Gallbladder**.

questions.question: Frequencies higher than the human audible limit of 20,000 Hz are classified as _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ultrasound**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The human auditory system is sensitive to a specific range of vibrations known as the **audible range**, which typically spans from **20 Hz to 20,000 Hz**.
 
• Sound waves with frequencies that surpass the upper limit of **20,000 Hz** (or **20 kHz**) are scientifically classified as **ultrasound** or **ultrasonic waves**.
 
• While these waves are physically identical to audible sound in terms of propagation, they are **inaudible** to the human ear because the **tympanic membrane** cannot vibrate at such high speeds.
 
• Many animals, including **bats**, **dolphins**, and **porpoises**, have the biological capability to produce and hear ultrasound, utilizing it for **echolocation** to hunt and navigate.
 
• The **Hertz (Hz)** is the standard **SI unit** of frequency, representing the number of **cycles per second**; thus, ultrasound involves over 20,000 vibrations every second.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Infrasound**:

 
 
• Refers to sound waves with a frequency **below 20 Hz**, which is the lower limit of human hearing.
 
• Sources include **seismic waves** from earthquakes, **volcanic eruptions**, and **ocean tides**.
 
• Large mammals like **elephants** and **rhinoceroses** communicate using infrasonic signals over vast distances.
 
 
 
• **Supersonic**:
 
 
• This term describes the **velocity** of an object rather than its frequency. An object is supersonic if it travels faster than the **speed of sound** (approximately **343 m/s** in air).
 
• When an aircraft reaches supersonic speeds, it produces a **sonic boom** due to the accumulation of shock waves.
 
 
 
• **Tones**:
 
 
• A **tone** is a sound that consists of a **single, pure frequency**. Most musical sounds are actually "notes," which combine a fundamental frequency with several **harmonics**.
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications of Ultrasound**:
 
 
• **Medical Imaging**: Utilized in **sonography** to visualize fetuses and internal organs without ionizing radiation.
 
• **SONAR**: Used by submarines and ships to detect **underwater obstacles** and measure the **depth of the sea**.
 
• **Industrial Cleaning**: High-frequency vibrations are used to remove contaminants from delicate **electronic components** and surgical instruments.

questions.question: Which rules define the process of identification, determination, and remediation of contaminated sites?

options.text: Environment Protection (Management of Contaminated Sites) Rules, 2025

questions.solution:
__Concept:__

The **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** has introduced a specific legal framework to address the long-standing issue of toxic and hazardous substance contamination in soil and water. These rules provide a systematic, time-bound procedure for handling sites that pose a risk to human health and the environment due to historical industrial activities or waste dumping.

__Key Points:__

__
 
• **Notification:** The rules were notified on **July 24, 2025**, under the powers conferred by the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**.
 
• **Process Stages:** The framework involves **Identification** (listing suspected sites), **Determination** (conducting preliminary and detailed assessments to confirm contamination levels), and **Remediation** (executing cleanup plans).
 
• **Accountability:** They incorporate the **'Polluter Pays'** principle, holding the responsible party liable for the costs of restoration.
 
• **Thresholds:** Sites are declared 'contaminated' if hazardous substance concentrations exceed the **response levels** specified in the rules.

Important Provisions:__

 
• The **State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs)** and **Pollution Control Committees (PCCs)** are responsible for the technical assessment and declaration of these sites.
 
• A **centralized online portal** is used to maintain an inventory of suspected, probable, and confirmed contaminated sites.
 
• Exclusions include sites affected strictly by **radioactive waste**, **mining operations**, or **marine oil spills**, which are governed by other specific acts unless contaminants exceed the response levels defined in these new rules.

questions.question: Which pollutant from the following is mainly responsible for the formation of acid rain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sulphur dioxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acid rain** refers to any form of precipitation, including rain, snow, or fog, that contains elevated levels of **nitric** and **sulphuric acids**.
 
• The primary chemical responsible for this phenomenon is **Sulphur dioxide (SO₂)**, which is released into the atmosphere through the **combustion of fossil fuels** (like coal and oil) in **power plants** and industrial boilers.
 
• Once in the atmosphere, **SO₂** reacts with **water vapor**, **oxygen**, and other chemicals to form **Sulphuric acid (H₂SO₄)**, which eventually falls to the ground as acid rain.
 
• While normal rainwater is slightly acidic with a **pH value** of about 5.6 (due to dissolved **Carbon dioxide**), acid rain typically has a **pH value** between 4.2 and 4.4.
 
• The environmental impact of acid rain includes the **acidification of aquatic environments**, damage to **forest vegetation**, and the **chemical weathering** of stone buildings and cultural monuments like the **Taj Mahal**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carbon monoxide (CO)**:

 
 
• A colorless, odorless, and highly toxic gas produced by the **incomplete combustion** of carbon-based fuels.
 
• It does not directly contribute to acid rain but poses significant health risks by reducing the **oxygen-carrying capacity** of blood.
 
 
 
• **Ozone (O₃)**:
 
 
• Found in the **troposphere**, it acts as a **secondary pollutant** and a major component of **photochemical smog**.
 
• While it helps catalyze some atmospheric oxidation processes, it is not a direct precursor to acid rain formation.
 
 
 
• **Ammonia (NH₃)**:
 
 
• An **alkaline gas** primarily emitted from **agricultural activities**, livestock management, and fertilizer use.
 
• In the atmosphere, it can act as a **buffering agent** to neutralize acidic compounds, though its deposition can still lead to soil and water issues.

• The performance is based on the **Kamba Ramayana**, the Tamil version of the epic written by the poet **Kambar**, spanning across 21 parts over 21 nights.
 
• The puppets are crafted from **deer skin**, meticulously perforated to create intricate patterns that project shadows onto a white cloth screen when illuminated by **coconut-shell oil lamps** (Chirathu).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Odisha**: Known for **Ravana Chhaya**, which uses puppets made from a single piece of leather without jointed limbs, resulting in opaque, non-colored shadows.
 
• **West Bengal**: Famous for various string and rod puppetry forms like **Putul Nautch** and **Danger Putul Nach**, often performed during local fairs.
 
• **Karnataka**: Practices **Togalu Gombeyaata**, a shadow puppet form similar to those in Andhra Pradesh but with distinct regional stylistic variations.

questions.question: The structural and functional unit of nature is _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ecosystem**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **ecosystem** is considered the **structural and functional unit of nature** because it encompasses the complex interactions between living organisms and their physical environment.
 
• The term was coined by **A.G. Tansley** in **1935** to describe a **self-regulating** and **self-sustaining** system.
 
• The **structural features** of an ecosystem consist of **biotic components** (producers, consumers, and decomposers) and **abiotic components** (temperature, light, water, and soil).
 
• The **functional aspects** of an ecosystem include **energy flow**, **nutrient cycling**, **productivity**, and **decomposition**, which ensure the continuity of life within a specific geographical area.
 
• Ecosystems can vary significantly in scale, ranging from a **small pond** or a single tree to vast **biomes** like tropical rainforests or the entire **biosphere**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Environment**:

 
 
• It refers to the **sum total** of all external conditions (physical, chemical, and biological) that surround and influence an organism.
 
• While it provides the setting for life, it lacks the specific **internal functional cycles** that define an ecosystem.
 
 
 
• **Cell**:
 
 
• The **cell** is the fundamental **structural and functional unit of life** or living organisms, not of nature as a whole.
 
• All living things are composed of cells, and the study of these units is known as **Cytology**.
 
 
 
• **Ecology**:
 
 
• **Ecology** is the **scientific study** of the relationships and interactions between organisms and their environment.
 
• The concept was popularized by **Ernst Haeckel** in **1866**, who defined it as the study of the economy of nature.

questions.question: What is the name of India’s first indigenous CRISPR-based gene therapy for Sickle Cell Disease, launched in November 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**BIRSA 101**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **BIRSA 101** is India’s first indigenous **CRISPR-Cas9** based gene therapy specifically designed to provide a curative treatment for **Sickle Cell Disease (SCD)**.
 
• Launched in **November 2025**, the therapy represents a major breakthrough in India’s **Atmanirbhar Bharat** initiative in the field of advanced **biotechnology** and **genomic medicine**.
 
• The therapy was developed through a collaborative research effort led by the **Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)** and the **Institute of Genomics and Integrative Biology (IGIB)**, aimed at making expensive gene treatments affordable for the Indian population.
 
• The treatment mechanism involves harvesting the patient’s own **hematopoietic stem cells**, using **CRISPR** technology to edit the **HBB gene** or induce **fetal hemoglobin (HbF)**, and then re-infusing them to produce healthy red blood cells.
 
• The naming of **BIRSA 101** pays tribute to the tribal leader **Birsa Munda**, reflecting the therapy's primary target demographic, as **Sickle Cell Disease** disproportionately affects **Scheduled Tribes** across the **tribal belt** of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sickle Cell Disease (SCD)**:

 
 
• It is an inherited **genetic blood disorder** where red blood cells become rigid and sickle-shaped, leading to **anemia**, **organ damage**, and **vaso-occlusive crises**.
 
• India has the second-highest global burden of **SCD**, with a high prevalence in states like **Madhya Pradesh**, **Gujarat**, and **Chhattisgarh**.
 
 
 
• **CRISPR Technology**:
 
 
• **Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats** (CRISPR) serves as a **molecular scissor** to edit DNA with high precision.
 
• It utilizes a **guide RNA** to identify the target genetic sequence and the **Cas9 enzyme** to execute the cut, allowing for the correction of **genetic mutations**.
 
 
 
• **National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission**:
 
 
• Announced in the **Union Budget 2023-24** and launched in **July 2023**, the mission aims to eliminate the disease as a public health threat by **2047**.
 
• The mission focuses on **universal screening** of approximately 7 crore people in the age group of 0−40 years in 17 high-burden states.

questions.question: How is a country's climate performance assessed in the CCPI (Climate Change Performance Index) 2025?

options.text: Based on renewable energy production statistics only
Combining emissions, energy use and expert-reviewed climate policy data
By analyzing only national emission targets and forest cover data
Through opinion polls and industrial development trends

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Combining emissions, energy use and expert-reviewed climate policy data**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI)** 2025 is an independent monitoring tool that evaluates the climate protection performance of **63 countries** and the **European Union**, which together account for more than **90%** of global greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• The assessment framework is divided into four distinct categories with specific weightings: **Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Emissions** (40%), **Renewable Energy** (20%), **Energy Use** (20%), and **Climate Policy** (20%).
 
• The **GHG Emissions** indicator tracks current emission levels, recent trends, and the alignment of national **2030 targets** with the **Paris Agreement** goal of limiting global warming to **1.5 degrees Celsius**.
 
• The **Climate Policy** component is unique because it incorporates qualitative data through **expert-reviewed** assessments provided by approximately **450 climate and energy experts** from non-governmental organizations and think tanks.
 
• The index uses a standardized methodology to provide a comparable score for each country, determining whether their progress is **Very High**, **High**, **Medium**, **Low**, or **Very Low**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Publication and Authorship**:

 
 
• The index is published annually by **Germanwatch**, the **NewClimate Institute**, and the **Climate Action Network (CAN) International**.
 
• The **CCPI 2025** report was officially released during the **COP29** summit held in **Baku, Azerbaijan**.
 
 
 
• **Methodological Limitations of Other Approaches**:
 
 
• **Renewable Energy statistics only**: This metric alone is insufficient as it does not account for the total carbon footprint or energy efficiency.
 
• **Forest Cover and National Targets**: While important for **carbon sequestration**, forest data is not a primary pillar of the CCPI, which prioritizes energy-related emissions and systemic **decarbonization**.
 
• **Opinion Polls**: Public sentiment is not a factor in the CCPI; it relies strictly on **hard data** from the **International Energy Agency (IEA)** and professional policy critiques.

= 28 + 4

= 32ⁿd

Position of **Rishabh** from the **right end** = 16th

Total number of people in the row = (Position of **Rishabh** from the **left end** + Position of **Rishabh** from the **right end**) − 1

= 32 + 16 − 1

= 47

Hence, the correct answer is **'Option 3'**.
